# 1. Load Curation File and Build Module-Level Leading-Edge Gene Sets

```{r load_curation_file}
# Load the a priori curated GO term file. Sheet names correspond to the
# three contrasts. Column header rows differ between sheets (some sheets
# have a "Parameters:" note row above the real header), hence the
# different `skip` values — confirmed by inspecting each sheet directly.

curation_eMPC_vs_iPSC <- read_excel(
  "~/Desktop/Tese/R/GSEA_GO_BP_curated_apriori.xlsx", sheet = "eMPC_vs_iPSC", skip = 2)
curation_EC_vs_eMPC   <- read_excel(
  "~/Desktop/Tese/R/GSEA_GO_BP_curated_apriori.xlsx", sheet = "EC_vs_eMPC", skip = 0)
curation_EC_vs_iPSC   <- read_excel(
  "~/Desktop/Tese/R/GSEA_GO_BP_curated_apriori.xlsx", sheet = "EC_vs_iPSC", skip = 0)

cat("Columns:", paste(colnames(curation_eMPC_vs_iPSC), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r extract_leading_edge}
# Extract leading edge genes from pathways marked "yes_apriori" in the
# a priori curation. Returns one row per (pathway, gene) pair, with
# biological_category and contrast carried along.
#
# Columns are renamed by position using base R (not tidyselect helpers),
# and all dplyr/tidyr calls are namespaced (dplyr::, tidyr::), for the
# same reasons documented in Molecular_Signatures.Rmd.

extract_leadinggene <- function(curation_df, contrast_name) {

  n <- ncol(curation_df)
  colnames(curation_df)[2] <- "include_apriori_std"
  colnames(curation_df)[3] <- "contrast_side_std"
  colnames(curation_df)[4] <- "biological_category_std"
  colnames(curation_df)[n] <- "leadingEdge_std"

  stopifnot(colnames(curation_df)[2] == "include_apriori_std")

  selected <- curation_df[
    !is.na(curation_df$include_apriori_std) &
    curation_df$include_apriori_std == "yes_apriori", ]

  cat(contrast_name, "— yes_apriori pathways:", nrow(selected), "\n")

  result <- selected %>%
    dplyr::select(
      pathway              = pathway,
      pathway_clean         = pathway_clean,
      biological_category   = biological_category_std,
      leadingEdge           = leadingEdge_std
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      contrast = contrast_name,
      leadingEdge = as.character(leadingEdge)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::separate_rows(leadingEdge, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
    dplyr::rename(gene = leadingEdge) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(gene), gene != "")

  return(result)
}

le_eMPC_vs_iPSC <- extract_leadinggene(curation_eMPC_vs_iPSC, "eMPC_vs_iPSC")
le_EC_vs_eMPC   <- extract_leadinggene(curation_EC_vs_eMPC,   "EC_vs_eMPC")
le_EC_vs_iPSC   <- extract_leadinggene(curation_EC_vs_iPSC,   "EC_vs_iPSC")

le_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(le_eMPC_vs_iPSC, le_EC_vs_eMPC, le_EC_vs_iPSC)

cat("\nTotal gene-pathway associations extracted:", nrow(le_all), "\n")
```

```{r build_module_gene_sets}
# Build the analytical gene set per biological module: the full union of
# leading-edge genes from ALL yes_apriori pathways in that module, across
# all three contrasts. No pathway subselection is applied — this mirrors
# the a priori curation logic itself, and avoids introducing a second,
# subjective selection criterion after pathway curation is already closed.

module_gene_sets <- le_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(biological_category) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(genes = list(unique(gene)), n_genes = dplyr::n_distinct(gene),
                    n_pathways = dplyr::n_distinct(pathway), .groups = "drop")

print(module_gene_sets[, c("biological_category","n_genes","n_pathways")])
```

# 2. Map Genes to STRING and Build Analytical Networks

```{r init_string_db}
# Initialize the STRING database connection.
# species = 9606: Homo sapiens
# score_threshold = 700: STRING "high confidence" interactions (STRING
#   uses a 0-1000 scale; 700 corresponds to a combined score of 0.7).
#   This is the analytical threshold, applied uniformly to every module,
#   fixed before results were inspected.
# Reference: Szklarczyk et al. 2023, Nucleic Acids Research, "The STRING
#   database in 2023: protein-protein association networks and
#   functional enrichment analyses for any sequenced genome of interest"
#   (STRING v12).

string_db <- STRINGdb$new(version = "12", species = 9606,
                           score_threshold = 700, input_directory = "")
```

```{r map_and_build_networks}
# For each module, map the full gene set to STRING identifiers and
# retrieve the analytical network (all mapped genes, no node reduction).
# This full network is used for all reported statistics (Section 3);
# node/edge reduction is applied only at the figure stage (Section 4).

map_module <- function(genes, module_name) {
  df <- data.frame(gene = genes, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  mapped <- string_db$map(df, "gene", removeUnmappedRows = TRUE)
  cat(module_name, "— submitted:", length(genes), "| mapped:", nrow(mapped), "\n")
  return(mapped)
}

module_mapped <- purrr::map2(
  module_gene_sets$genes, module_gene_sets$biological_category,
  map_module
)
names(module_mapped) <- module_gene_sets$biological_category
```

# 3. Network Statistics per Module

```{r network_statistics}
# Report, for each module, the statistics of the FULL analytical network
# (never the reduced visualization subset): submitted genes, mapped
# genes, nodes, edges, expected edges, and PPI enrichment p-value
# (string_db$get_ppi_enrichment tests whether the observed number of
# edges exceeds what would be expected for a random gene set of the
# same size, drawn from the full STRING network).

get_module_stats <- function(mapped_df, submitted_n, module_name) {
  if (nrow(mapped_df) < 2) {
    cat(module_name, ": fewer than 2 mapped genes, skipping\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  enrichment <- string_db$get_ppi_enrichment(mapped_df$STRING_id)

  data.frame(
    module           = module_name,
    submitted_genes  = submitted_n,
    mapped_genes     = nrow(mapped_df),
    nodes            = nrow(mapped_df),
    edges            = enrichment$edges,
    expected_edges   = enrichment$lambda,
    ppi_enrichment_p = enrichment$enrichment
  )
}

network_stats <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  list(module_mapped, module_gene_sets$n_genes, names(module_mapped)),
  get_module_stats
)

print(network_stats)
write_xlsx(list("network_statistics" = network_stats), path = "STRING_network_statistics.xlsx")
```

```{r hub_genes}
# Top hub genes per module by degree (number of connections), calculated
# from the FULL analytical network (score >= 0.7) via igraph.
# STRINGdb::get_interactions() returns each interaction twice, so
# duplicated interactions are removed before building the graph
# (A-B and B-A are treated as the same interaction). Without this step,
# all degrees were doubled (the ranking was unaffected).

# Display names (American spelling, sentence case), as in the
# Molecular Signatures figures
module_display_names <- c(
  "mesoderm development"                            = "Mesoderm development",
  "embryonic patterning and morphogenesis"          = "Embryonic patterning and morphogenesis",
  "mesenchymal development"                         = "Mesenchymal development",
  "epithelial-mesenchymal transition"               = "Epithelial\u2013mesenchymal transition",
  "cardiovascular and endocardial development"      = "Cardiovascular and endocardial development",
  "developmental signalling"                        = "Developmental signaling",
  "pluripotency / stem cell maintenance"            = "Stem cell population maintenance",
  "endothelial specification"                       = "Endothelial specification",
  "VEGF signaling and endothelial response"         = "VEGF signaling and endothelial response",
  "angiogenesis / vasculogenesis"                   = "Angiogenesis / vasculogenesis",
  "cell adhesion and cell-matrix interaction"       = "Cell adhesion and cell\u2013matrix interaction",
  "extracellular matrix organization / remodelling" = "Extracellular matrix organization / remodeling",
  "mechanotransduction / shear stress"              = "Mechanotransduction / shear stress",
  "vascular homeostasis / fluid regulation"         = "Vascular homeostasis / fluid regulation",
  "hemostasis / coagulation"                        = "Hemostasis / coagulation",
  "immune / inflammatory response"                  = "Immune / inflammatory response"
)

# Check: every module has a display name (expect character(0))
print(setdiff(trimws(names(module_mapped)), names(module_display_names)))

# Build an undirected graph without duplicated interactions
build_module_graph <- function(mapped_df) {
  interactions <- string_db$get_interactions(mapped_df$STRING_id)
  if (nrow(interactions) == 0) return(NULL)
  interactions_unique <- interactions %>%
    dplyr::mutate(id1 = pmin(from, to), id2 = pmax(from, to)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(id1, id2, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::select(from = id1, to = id2, dplyr::everything(), -dplyr::any_of(c("id1", "id2")))
  igraph::graph_from_data_frame(interactions_unique, directed = FALSE)
}

get_hub_genes <- function(mapped_df, module_name, top_n = 10) {
  g <- build_module_graph(mapped_df)
  if (is.null(g)) return(NULL)

  deg <- igraph::degree(g)
  deg_df <- data.frame(STRING_id = names(deg), degree = deg) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(mapped_df[, c("gene","STRING_id")], by = "STRING_id") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(degree)) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = top_n) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(module = module_name,
                  module_display = unname(module_display_names[trimws(module_name)]))

  return(deg_df[, c("module","module_display","gene","degree")])
}

# Check: number of unique interactions per module should match the
# edges reported by get_ppi_enrichment() in network_stats (expect all TRUE)
edges_check <- purrr::map_int(module_mapped, function(df) {
  g <- build_module_graph(df)
  if (is.null(g)) 0L else igraph::ecount(g)
})
print(data.frame(module = names(edges_check),
                 edges_graph = edges_check,
                 edges_stats = network_stats$edges[match(names(edges_check), network_stats$module)],
                 match = edges_check == network_stats$edges[match(names(edges_check), network_stats$module)]))

hub_genes_all <- purrr::map2_dfr(module_mapped, names(module_mapped), get_hub_genes)
write_xlsx(list("hub_genes" = hub_genes_all), path = "STRING_hub_genes.xlsx")
print(hub_genes_all)
```

# 4. Network Visualization

```{r draw_networks, fig.width=9, fig.height=9}
# Fixed visualization rule, defined before inspecting individual network
# sizes: modules with <=80 mapped nodes are shown in full; modules with
# >80 nodes are reduced to the top 25 nodes by degree. Degree is computed
# from the FULL analytical network (score >= 0.7) without duplicated
# interactions (build_module_graph, hub_genes chunk). Figure edges are
# always filtered to score >= 0.9 (STRINGdb score_threshold = 900),
# regardless of module size. This rule is applied identically to every
# module — no module-specific adjustment based on how the figure looks.
# Titles use the display module names (module_display_names).
# add_summary = FALSE removes the summary text that plot_network() prints
# by default (protein/interaction counts and p-value of the visualization
# network), which differs from the analytical statistics reported in the text.

string_db_highconf <- STRINGdb$new(version = "12", species = 9606,
                                    score_threshold = 900, input_directory = "")

draw_module_network <- function(mapped_df, module_name) {
  if (nrow(mapped_df) < 2) return(invisible(NULL))

  display_name <- unname(module_display_names[trimws(module_name)])

  if (nrow(mapped_df) > 80) {
    g <- build_module_graph(mapped_df)
    deg <- igraph::degree(g)
    top_ids <- names(sort(deg, decreasing = TRUE))[1:25]
    plot_set <- mapped_df[mapped_df$STRING_id %in% top_ids, ]
    cat(display_name, ": >80 nodes, showing top 25 by degree\n")
  } else {
    plot_set <- mapped_df
    cat(display_name, ": <=80 nodes, showing full network\n")
  }

  # Increase top margin (bottom, left, top, right) to make room for the title
  par(mar = c(1, 1, 6, 1))
  string_db_highconf$plot_network(plot_set$STRING_id, add_summary = FALSE)
  title(main = display_name, line = 4, cex.main = 1.3)
}

purrr::walk2(module_mapped, names(module_mapped), draw_module_network)
```

# 5. Export Mapped Gene Lists per Module

```{r export_mapped_genes}
# Export the full mapped gene list per module (STRING identifiers +
# original gene symbols), for reference and reproducibility.

mapped_export <- purrr::map2(
  module_mapped, names(module_mapped),
  function(df, name) dplyr::mutate(df, module = name)
) %>% dplyr::bind_rows()

write_xlsx(list("mapped_genes_by_module" = mapped_export), path = "STRING_mapped_genes.xlsx")
cat("Exported STRING_mapped_genes.xlsx —", nrow(mapped_export), "rows\n")
```
